arxiv-1909-13588.creator: Pavel ETINGOF and Douglas STRYKER
arxiv-1909-13588.description: Abstract We develop a theory of short star-products for filtered quantizations of graded Poisson algebras, introduced in 2016 by Beem, Peelaers and Rastelli for algebras of regular functions on hyperKähler cones in the context of 3-dimensional N = 4 N=4 superconformal field theories [Beem C., Peelaers W., Rastelli L., Comm. Math. Phys. 354 (2017), 345–392].

arxiv-2109-13691.title: BACKWARD RAUZY-VEECH ALGORITHM AND HORIZONTAL SADDLE CONNECTIONS MSC classification: 37E05, 37E35
arxiv-2109-13691.creator: Przemysław Berk
arxiv-2109-13691.description: Abstract . We study the combinatorial and dynamical properties of translations surfaces with horizontal saddle connections from the point of view of backward Rauzy-Veech induction. Namely, we prove that although the horizontal saddle connections do not rule out existence of the infinite orbit under backward Rauzy-Veech algorithm, they disallow the ∞ \infty - completeness of such orbit.

arxiv-2111-02197.title: The Psychological Gains from COVID-19 Vaccination: Who Benefits the Most? Thanks: Manuel Bagues, University of Warwick, CEPR, IZA and J-Pal; email: manuel.bagues@warwick.ac.uk; Velichka Dimitrova, University of Warwick; email: velichka.dimitrova.1@warwick.ac.uk. We thank Andrew Oswald, Thiemo Fetzer
arxiv-2111-02197.creator: Manuel Bagues Velichka Dimitrova
arxiv-2111-02197.description: Abstract We quantify the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on psychological well-being using information from a large-scale panel survey representative of the UK population. Exploiting exogenous variation in the timing of vaccinations, we find that vaccination increases psychological well-being (GHQ-12) by 0.12 standard deviation, compensating for around one half of the overall decrease caused by the pandemic.

arxiv-2210-03493.title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
arxiv-2210-03493.creator: Zhuosheng Zhang, Aston Zhang, Mu Li, Alex Smola
arxiv-2210-03493.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can perform complex reasoning by generating intermediate reasoning steps. Providing these steps for prompting demonstrations is called chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. CoT prompting has two major paradigms. One leverages a simple prompt like “Let’s think step by step” to facilitate step-by-step thinking before answering a question.

arxiv-2303-05379.title: Orbital stability of two circumbinary planets around misaligned eccentric binaries 2022 Orbital stability of two circumbinary planets around misaligned eccentric binaries – References
arxiv-2303-05379.creator: Cheng Chen, Stephen H. Lubow, Rebecca G. Martin, C. J. Nixon
arxiv-2303-05379.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cheng Chen, Stephen H. Lubow, Rebecca G. Martin, C. J. Nixon. With n n -body simulations we investigate the stability of tilted circumbinary planetary systems consisting of two nonzero mass planets. The planets are initially in circular orbits that are coplanar to each other, as would be expected if they form in a flat but tilted circumbinary gas disc and decouple from the disc within a time difference that is much less than the disc nodal precession period.

arxiv-2402-05302.title: Training DNN Models over Heterogeneous Clusters with Optimal Performance DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: XXXXXX; XXXXX; XXXXX CCS: Computing methodologies Distributed computing CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Computing methodologies Heterogeneous computing
arxiv-2402-05302.creator: Chengyi Nie, Jessica Maghakian, Zhenhua Liu
arxiv-2402-05302.description: Abstract . Adjusting batch sizes and adaptively tuning other hyperparameters can significantly speed up deep neural network (DNN) training. Despite the ubiquity of heterogeneous clusters, existing adaptive DNN training techniques solely consider homogeneous environments. Optimizing distributed DNN training over heterogeneous clusters is technically challenging, and directly adapting existing techniques results in low utilization and poor performance.

arxiv-2410-08906.title: Oversights in Characterising Heralded Single Photon Sources
arxiv-2410-08906.creator: Hugh Barrett 1,2,∗ , Imad I. Faruque 2
arxiv-2410-08906.description: Abstract The development of ideal sources is a fundamental challenge for the practical implementation of integrated photonic technologies for quantum applications. In this paper we analyse the state-of-the-art in heralded single photon sources; pointing out inconsistencies in the how key parameters, such as brightness and heralding efficiency, are characterised.

arxiv-2503-20141.title: On affine homogeneous polynomial centrosymmetric matrices
arxiv-2503-20141.creator: Miriam Manoel, Leandro Nery
arxiv-2503-20141.description: Abstract We explore a class of centrosymmetric matrices whose entries are polynomials in two variables, referred to as DNA matrices. Our motivation stems from an unexpected connection between these matrices and invariant polynomials under the action of a Lorentz rotation on the plane.

arxiv-2507-15909.title: Bayesian implementation of Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation for uncertainty quantification in causal effect estimation Journal: Expert Systems with Applications
arxiv-2507-15909.creator: Saideep Nannapaneni, Joseph Sakaya, Kyle Caron, Pedro HM Albuquerque, Zaid Tashman
arxiv-2507-15909.description: Abstract Robust decision making involves making decisions in the presence of uncertainty and is often used in critical domains such as healthcare, supply chains, and finance. Causality plays a crucial role in decision-making as it predicts the change in an outcome (usually a key performance indicator) due to a treatment (also called an intervention).

pmc-10532020.title: Predicting Treatment Response in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases: Cross-Sectional Imaging Markers
pmc-10532020.creator: Irene Mignini, Rossella Maresca, Maria Elena Ainora, Luigi Larosa, Franco Scaldaferri, Antonio Gasbarrini, Maria Assunta Zocco, Matteo Cimino
pmc-10532020.description: Therapeutic options for inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) have largely expanded in the last decades, both in Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, including multiple biological drugs targeting different inflammation pathways. However, choosing the best treatment and timing for each patient is still an undeniable challenge for IBD physicians due to the marked heterogeneity among patients and disease behavior.

pmc-10582377.title: A potential role of mechano-gated potassium channels in meningioma-related seizures
pmc-10582377.creator: Ivan Bogdanović, Miloš Opačić, Vladimir Baščarević, Savo Raičević, Rosanda Ilić, Danica Grujičić, Ivan Spasojević, Aleksandar J Ristić
pmc-10582377.description: Every third patient with intracranial meningioma develops seizures of poorly understood etiology. Tumor and peritumoral edema may exert mechanical pressure on the cortex that may affect mechano-gated potassium channels - KCNK2 and KCNK4. These channels regulate neuron excitability and have been related to seizures in some other conditions.

pmc-10739342.title: PILOTING COMMUNICATION TOOLS TO ENHANCE RESIDENT/FAMILY ENGAGEMENT IN NURSING HOMES CARE CONFERENCES
pmc-10739342.creator: Jingxi Li, Alexa Roscizewski, Terra Warthen, Elizabeth Cox, Tonya Roberts
pmc-10739342.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Nursing home (NH) regulations mandate resident and family engagement in care planning. Additionally, our previous research indicated residents/families want to be involved in care decisions. Care conferences are an important opportunity for residents/families to engage in decision-making. However, there is a lack of guidance or tools to support their engagement and a dearth of research on the most effective approaches to doing so.

pmc-11306352.title: Molecular folding governs switchable singlet oxygen photoproduction in porphyrin-decorated bistable rotaxanes
pmc-11306352.creator: Jan Riebe, Benedikt Bädorf, Sarah Löffelsender, Matias E Gutierrez Suburu, María Belén Rivas Aiello, Cristian A Strassert, Stefan Grimme, Jochen Niemeyer
pmc-11306352.description: Rotaxanes are mechanically interlocked molecules where a ring (macrocycle) is threaded onto a linear molecule (thread). The position of the macrocycle on different stations on the thread can be controlled in response to external stimuli, making rotaxanes applicable as molecular switches.

pmc-11342367.title: Picosecond Femtojoule Resistive Switching in Nanoscale VO2 Memristors
pmc-11342367.creator: Sebastian
pmc-11342367.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Beyond-Moore computing technologies are expected to provide a sustainable alternative to the von Neumann approach not only due to their down-scaling potential but also via exploiting device-level functional complexity at the lowest possible energy consumption. The dynamics of the Mott transition in correlated electron oxides, such as vanadium dioxide, has been identified as a rich and reliable source of such functional complexity. However, its full potential in high-speed and low-power operation has been largely unexplored.

pmc-11452091.title: Road-traffic noise exposure and coronary atherosclerosis in the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study (SCAPIS)
pmc-11452091.creator: Marat Murzabekov, Åsa Persson, Christian Asker, Karl Kilbo Edlund, Charlotta Eriksson, Tomas Jernberg, Peter Molnar, Anna Oudin, Andrei Pyko, Jenny Lindvall, Mare Lõhmus, Kerstin Persson Waye, Johan Nilsson Sommar, Leo Stockfelt, Mårten Spanne, Magnus Svartengren, Mikael Ögren, Göran Pershagen, Pett
pmc-11452091.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:Road-traffic noise may influence the development of cardiovascular events such as stroke and myocardial infarction, but etiological mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to assess the relationship between long-term road-traffic noise exposure and coronary atherosclerosis in Sweden.Methods:In the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study (SCAPIS) cohort, including 30,154 subjects aged 50–65 years, recruited between 2013 and 2018, coronary atherosclerosis was measured based on computer tomography (CT) scans as coronary artery calcium score, segment involvement score (SIS), and non-calcified plaques (NCP) at enrollment.

pmc-11643950.title: C/Ni/N Nanocomposites Based on Hydrolysis Lignin: Synthesis, Study of Structural and Magnetic Properties
pmc-11643950.creator: Ihor Bordun, Dariusz Calus, Ewelina Szymczykiewicz, Myroslav Malovanyy, Nazar Nahurskyi, Anatoliy Borysiuk, Yuriy Kulyk, Vasileios Tzitzios
pmc-11643950.description: A two-step method for the synthesis of C/Ni/N nanocomposites based on hydrolysis lignin from wood chemical processing waste is proposed. These nanocomposites were found to have a well-developed porous structure with a wide pore size distribution. It was shown that doping hydrolysis lignin with urea-derived nitrogen leads to the appearance of ferromagnetic behavior in the carbon material.

pmc-12750503.title: E.coli-derived CsgA-peptides stimulate cytokine production in microglia and lead to transient changes in neocortical Aβ-levels in pre-plaque APPSWE/PS1ΔE9 and wild type mice
pmc-12750503.creator: Leda Mygind, Gabriel Jensen, Victoria Neesgaard, Katrine Tækker Krohn, Sergi Torres Puig, Anders Boysen, Sussanne Petersen, Kate Lykke Lambertsen, Athanasios Metaxas, Michael Kemp, Jakob Møller-Jensen, Bente Finsen
pmc-12750503.description: Epidemiological and pre-clinical data propose that infections can accelerate the cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other dementias. The implication of infectious agents, and especially the role of E.coli and other amyloid-peptide producing bacteria, on the development and progression of cerebral amyloidosis and neuroinflammation, both key neuropathological characteristics of AD, has only been studied to a limited extent.

pmc-13246779.title: Navigating polymorph generation and distilled-potential development via entropy-symmetry landscapes for metal plasticity mechanisms
pmc-13246779.creator: Zeyuan Li, Taiqiao Liu, Xuhao Wan, Songpeng Zhao, Zhaofu Zhang, E Zhou, Wei Yu, Yijing Zuo, John Robertson, Sheng Liu, Yuzheng Guo
pmc-13246779.description: Artificial intelligence has advanced crystal design, yet unifying crystal structure prediction with thermodynamics-driven structure-property modelling remains challenging owing to divergent methodological foundations. Here we show that an integrated framework called PolymorphGen‑MLPKD, driven by physically meaningful entropy-symmetry landscapes, enables targeted generation of polymorphs and concurrent structure-property modelling.

pmc-13380910.title: Feasibility of Home-Based Electromagnetic Navigation-Guided Nasojejunal Tube Placement in a High-Risk Bedridden Elderly: A Case Report
pmc-13380910.creator: Ningxuan Liu, Meng Hong
pmc-13380910.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the feasibility and clinical outcomes of a nurse‑performed, home‑based electromagnetic navigation‑guided nasojejunal tube placement in a high‑risk bedridden elderly patient who was unable to be transported to hospital.MethodsWe present a case of an 89-year-old male with long-term bedridden status and high aspiration risk. A qualified nurse performed electromagnetic navigation-guided nasojejunal tube insertion in the patient’s home environment.

pmc-13491816.title: CALR-dependent endoplasmic reticulum N-glycoprotein maturation promotes Japanese encephalitis virus entry and replication
pmc-13491816.creator: Yonghui Zhang, Jinyan Zhang, Rui Jiang, Jingpei Han, Hailong Liu, Yuan Wang, Liuxing Qin, Zishi Guo, Yuqing Yang, Jinxue Ruan, Xinyun Li, Xiangmin Li, Kun Han, Ping Qian, Shengsong Xie
pmc-13491816.description: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone machinery participates in multiple stages of viral infection, from entry through assembly and release. However, how ER-resident quality-control mechanisms shape cellular permissiveness to Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) remains unclear. Here, we identify the ER-resident chaperone calreticulin (CALR) as a key host factor that promotes cellular permissiveness to JEV infection.

pmc-13552388.title: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of the Intradialytic Hypotension–Related Health Beliefs Scale for Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis
pmc-13552388.creator: Ting Luo, Guangyi Yang, Siying Li, Zhenye Mu, Hongdan Wang, Min Yang
pmc-13552388.description: PurposeTo develop the Intradialytic Hypotension (IDH)–Related Health Beliefs Scale for patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) and preliminarily evaluate its psychometric properties.MethodsA multistage scale-development study combined literature review, patient interviews, Delphi consultation, and pretesting. Convenience sampling recruited 451 patients from four tertiary hospitals in China. Before item analysis, participants were randomly divided into development (n=226) and validation (n=225) samples.
